explanations: pay_date is an epoch value in seconds like period_start and period_end, but it is passed straight to new Date, which expects milliseconds. A pay date like 1767225600 becomes a Date in January 1970, and nothing rejects it, so every imported payslip carries a wrong pay date. It should go through fromEpochSeconds like the other two timestamps.

Money as integer strings converted with BigInt keeps exact values regardless of size, and the strict equality balance check depends on exact arithmetic. bigint is not faster, JSON supports negative numbers, and strings are not smaller.
The loop reads the existing value with deductions.get(d.code) ?? 0n and adds the new amount, so duplicates accumulate into 7500. Nothing overwrites, checks uniqueness, or keeps duplicate Map keys.

mapPayslip errors are caught per payslip, pushed onto summary.rejected, and the loop continues; pagination follows next_cursor regardless. Only client errors (not caught here) would abort, and there is no retry logic.
